**The meaning of the hadith**
Islam built the society of the Muslims on a firm foundation of brotherhood and mutual support among them. Allah the Exalted said: { إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ } (The believers are but brothers) [Al-Hujurat: 10].

… And he tells us that whoever strives to meet the need of his Muslim brother, Allah the Exalted will help him and make it easy for his own need to be met.

And whoever helps a Muslim in a hardship of this world that has befallen him, that is, in a sorrow that weighs on his soul, or in one of the misfortunes of this world, until his sorrow and misfortune are gone, Allah will remove from him a misfortune and one of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection.

📖 From the Hadith Encyclopedia — Dorar.net.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Iyad see when he saw Grandma Safiyya walking to the corner shop? And what did he do?
2. What did his father tell him about the meaning of "May Allah help you, as you have helped me"?
3. When the bike came back, do we say that Iyad helped Grandma so that he would get something back? (No; he helped her for the sake of Allah, and Allah helps whoever helps his brother in whatever way He wills and whenever He wills, in this world or in the Hereafter.)

**This week's exercise**
Every day your child asks someone in the family or one of the neighbours, with you beside them, "What do you need?" and then helps them with a small need: carrying a bag, fetching something, or watering a plant.
